blocks.text: MOBILIZE
Pre-engagement
Mobilize before engagement: confirm sponsors, owners, data access, sample availability, security contacts, and first journey hypothesis.
Named owners and access readiness authorize discovery.
Evidence / output
Sponsor and owner map; access readiness; first journey hypothesis.

DISCOVER &
DEFINE
Weeks 1–4
Discover and define, weeks 1–4: observe the journey, validate baseline, map system constraints, define a thin release, and agree acceptance measures.
Agree the baseline and acceptance measures before implementation.
Evidence / output
Validated baseline; thin-release definition; acceptance checklist.

BUILD &
PROVE
Weeks 5–10
Build and prove, weeks 5–10: implement the first journey, interface contract, access controls, telemetry, and test evidence in a nonproduction environment.
Use test and control evidence to assess pilot readiness.
Evidence / output
Implemented journey; interface contract; telemetry and test evidence.

PILOT &
ADAPT
Weeks 11–14
Pilot and adapt, weeks 11–14: run a bounded cohort, rehearse exception handling, compare measures to validated baseline, and resolve readiness findings.
Resolve findings before a steering expansion decision.
Evidence / output
Cohort observations; baseline comparison; owned readiness findings.

SCALE &
TRANSITION
Weeks 15–20
Scale and transition, weeks 15–20: expand only after steering gate, transfer operational ownership, and prioritize the next journey from measured evidence.
Accept operational ownership before further expansion.
Evidence / output
Transfer acceptance; prioritized next journey; steering decision.

blocks.text: Discover and define
Discovery converts an unvalidated baseline and broad problem into an owned thin-release definition.

Baseline validation

blocks.text: Journey responsibility
Control and boundary
Proposed behavior
Evidence / owner
01  Participants
Keep the entry channel, service queue and processing responsibilities visible as separate participants.
Represent requester portal, shared operations queue, and three downstream processing systems as distinct participants.
Confirm business and system owners; trace where transaction state is created and changed.
02  Intake validation
Check completeness at entry and route missing information back to the requester with a clear reason.
Show intake validation and missing-information return path while alternate intake remains available during transition.
Business owner confirms required information, alternate intake and the return-path decision.
03  Ownership
A case must have an accountable business owner, a service queue and a known escalation route.
Assign business owner, service queue, and escalation route at each case state; capture decision and reassignment reasons.
Record state transitions, decision rationale and reassignment reasons in the case history.
04  Case trace
Preserve transaction ownership in existing processing systems until an explicit migration decision.

Use the consistent case identifier to link status, access, processing events, and audit history. The case identifier and event trace are proposed design responsibilities, not a committed vendor or platform selection.
Architecture and control owners define the identifier, access boundaries and auditable event linkage.
05  Exception handling
Separate the exception reason from the case state so operational action and genuine new demand remain distinguishable.
Show technical failure, waiting decision, incomplete intake, and genuine demand as distinct exception categories.
Record the exception reason, recovery owner and decision required to resume processing.

blocks.text: 01  Mobilize and sequence
Mobilization readiness depends on sponsors, owners, data access, sample availability, security contacts, and a first journey hypothesis.
Access delays, unremediated source data, vendor constraints, or material control changes can move the sequence.
02  Authorize pilot
Proceed to pilot only after owners accept test evidence, critical control findings are resolved, operations can execute runbooks, and rollback is rehearsed.
Additional journeys, integrations, and operating hours require separate scope decisions.
03  Decide expansion
Proceed to expansion only when validated baseline and pilot data support the decision; if evidence is weak or conditions change, adjust scope and retain the existing service.
No expansion decision is implied before evidence and readiness gates are met.

ILLUSTRATIVE • FICTIONAL CASE-FLOW MODERNIZATION
01  WORKFLOW EXPERIENCE
Experience layer covers the requester portal, agent workspace, and supervisor decisions.
02  ORCHESTRATION LAYER
Orchestration layer covers case state and rules, exception routing, and integration events.
03  PLATFORM FOUNDATION
Platform layer covers identity and access, case data and audit, telemetry, and support.

These are proposed responsibilities, not a prescribed vendor product stack. Existing systems remain transaction owners; the diagram does not imply consolidation. Interface feasibility, data authority, retention rules, and control design require client review.

blocks.text: The governance band defines product ownership, data stewardship, and change gates.
The security band spans identity, least privilege, data retention, and monitoring.
Requester portal
Validate intake and show missing information while retaining alternate routes during transition.
Agent workspace
Make case state, assigned queue, evidence and next action visible to the people doing the work.
Supervisor decisions
Review waiting decisions, escalation reasons and reassignment choices with accountable owners.
Exception routing
Distinguish missing information, waiting decisions, technical failure and genuine new demand.
Case state and rules
Avoid an additional ungoverned copy of case state.
Integration events
A canonical identifier and published event contracts connect the journey without requiring one platform in the first release.
Case data and audit
Keep transaction ownership in existing processing systems until an explicit migration decision.
Identity and access
Apply identity, least privilege and retention controls across the case journey and its evidence.
Telemetry and support
Observe processing and recovery events; connect service evidence to accountable operations owners.

ILLUSTRATIVE PROCESS PATHS
Case decisions and release changes need two governed review paths
01  Case decision path
02  Change and release path

The case path validates intake and establishes the consistent case identifier. It assigns a business owner and service queue before a case-state decision. It routes exceptions to an explicit escalation path and records reassignment reasons.

The change path logs a proposed change and brings architecture and control owners into review. It requires test evidence and operational readiness review before the steering release gate. Release, hold, rollback, and recovery responsibilities must be explicit.
